Preregistered or expected: Chest measurements were primary and near-eye measurements a robustness repeat.
Analysis used: Near-eye measurements are primary; chest measurements are complementary and placements are not pooled.

Preregistered or expected: Protocol eligibility and fixed daily/hourly coverage exclusions defined the sample.
Analysis used: Verified participant-day coverage is followed by metric-specific support; every fitted model reports its exact rows and support hours.

Preregistered or expected: Logged non-wear and sleep exclusions were applied without a fully specified state hierarchy.
Analysis used: Diary sleep has precedence, invalid non-wear is masked consistently, and sleep measurements are described as the bedside environment rather than ocular exposure.

Preregistered or expected: Values above 120,000 lx were to be removed.
Analysis used: The verified analytical melEDI signal retains values strictly below 100,000 lx.

Preregistered or expected: The level metric used the five darkest hours.
Analysis used: The specified metric is the mean melEDI during the darkest 10 hours.

Preregistered or expected: The timing outcome was the midpoint of the longest period above 250 lx.
Analysis used: The registered midpoint of the longest qualifying period is retained. Mean timing above 250 lx melEDI is a distinct circular duration-weighted metric and is labelled as an adapted sensitivity; period construction follows verified continuity and support rules.

Preregistered or expected: One model included both site and latitude.
Analysis used: Because each site has one latitude, fixed-site and linear-latitude models are fitted separately on identical rows and compared for adequacy.

Preregistered or expected: Photoperiod adjustment was specified for duration metrics.
Analysis used: Photoperiod is included in the common model implementation for all 17 metrics.

Preregistered or expected: Linear mixed models were specified generically.
Analysis used: Each metric uses its specified Gaussian transformation or Tweedie log-link response model.

Preregistered or expected: False-discovery-rate control was required within H1 but the exact vectors were not specified.
Analysis used: Four separate complete 17-test Benjamini–Hochberg families are used for site, photoperiod, latitude, and site-versus-latitude adequacy.

Preregistered or expected: Site coefficients were reported without a fixed hierarchical follow-up rule.
Analysis used: Only after a supported overall site test, each site is compared with the equally weighted overall site mean and the site contrasts are adjusted within metric.

Preregistered or expected: Conditional R² and significance-dependent component summaries were used without joint interval estimation or exact model-specific sample reporting.
Analysis used: Marginal and conditional R², participant-associated share, and non-overlapping term part-R² summaries use 1,000 successful joint bootstrap refits in the full run and 95% intervals; exact model-specific samples are reported.

Preregistered or expected: Fixed-effect structures had been compared using REML-derived criteria.
Analysis used: Gaussian fixed-effect comparisons use maximum likelihood; final Gaussian estimation uses REML where applicable.

Preregistered or expected: The intended relation between worn exposure and sleep-period environmental measurement was implicit.
Analysis used: The 24-hour record retains both constructs but keeps their interpretations distinct.

Preregistered or expected: MDER summarizes momentary melEDI-to-photopic-illuminance ratios; the preregistration did not specify a ratio-of-integrals definition.
Analysis used: MDER is the arithmetic mean of viable one-minute melEDI-to-photopic-illuminance ratios. Both channels must be finite and strictly positive, and at least 720 viable minutes are required on the complete 1,440-minute local wall-clock grid.

Preregistered or expected: Incomplete repeated-day support could enter the dynamics metrics.
Analysis used: Dynamics metrics use verified temporal support and report participant-level model rows plus contributing participant-days.

Preregistered or expected: Missing intervals could be bridged or incomplete windows summarized.
Analysis used: Windows and continuous periods use support, continuity, gap, wrapping, and tie rules fixed before modelling.

Preregistered or expected: Dose could be a partial sum without a defined support denominator.
Analysis used: Dose is time-sensitive and retained only with the specified interval support.

Preregistered or expected: A single local time axis and one assumed source epoch were used.
Analysis used: Absolute time governs ordering and duration, local wall time governs clock metrics, repeated fall-back bins are handled explicitly, and each source epoch is respected.

Preregistered or expected: The preregistration uses coverage and signal-validity rules but does not specify exclusion of an otherwise eligible complete exact-zero melEDI day.
Analysis used: An otherwise eligible participant-day is excluded only when every finite one-minute melEDI value is exactly 0 lx; individual zeros remain valid and retaining these days is a sensitivity analysis.

Preregistered or expected: The label implied a single three-hour window before sleep.
Analysis used: The outcome is calendar-day cumulative time below 10 lx melEDI across every diary-defined pre-sleep interval; values strictly above six hours trigger a diagnostic warning but are not capped.

Preregistered or expected: The clock response was linearized around noon.
Analysis used: The primary conversion subtracts 24 hours only for values strictly after 16:00; the noon cut is a registered same-row sensitivity.
